issues.message: Tags are normalized on write: trimmed, lower-cased, de-duplicated, at most 20 per book and 40 characters each (violations are 400). They are accepted as an optional `tags` array on POST /books and returned as `tags` in every book view (including the book summary embedded in a loan).

"Search can additionally filter by one tag" is implemented as a new `tag` query parameter on GET /books (exact, case-insensitive tag match; combined with q/title/author/isbn), not as a second search dimension. Since the spec gives no endpoint to change tags after creation, posting an existing ISBN now also merges the new payload's tags into the existing book (copies are still the only thing counted).

summary:
Implemented book tags per books.md:9.

Service:
- `BookRecord`/`BookView` gained `tags: string[]`, normalized (trimmed, lower-cased, de-duplicated) via a new `readOptionalStringList` validator (max 20 tags, 40 chars each, non-array or non-string entries are 400).
- `POST /books` accepts optional `tags`; when the ISBN already exists the copies are still merged and the new tags are merged into the existing record.
- `GET /books` gained a `tag` filter (case-insensitive exact match, combinable with `q`/`title`/`author`/`isbn`); `GET /books/{id}` and loan views also carry the tags.
- Added `normalizeTag` helper and `BookFilter.tag`.

Client (`libctl`, stdlib only):
- `add-book --tag TAG` (repeatable) and `search [query] --tag TAG` (query now optional when a tag is given); book tables have a new `TAGS` column.

Docs & tests:
- README documents tag normalization limits, the `tag` filter, tag merging and the new client flags.
- 7 new service tests in `test/books.test.ts` (storage/listing, defaults, tag filter incl. trimming and empty result, combined query+tag, merge on duplicate ISBN, validation errors, tags inside loan views) and a CLI tag test. Full suite: 62 tests, 0 failures. Build artifacts, node_modules and package-lock removed before finishing.

Warnings raised: the tag filter is modelled as a `tag` query parameter; tag merging on duplicate ISBN is an assumption since the specs define no separate "edit tags" operation.
